title: Rectangular base
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to [0.0, 0.0, -90.0] and a translation vector of [0.0, 0.0375, 0.0]. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on a new face by creating a loop of four lines. The first line starts at [0.0, 0.0] and ends at [0.75, 0.0]. The second line starts at [0.75, 0.0] and ends at [0.75, 0.0375]. The third line starts at [0.75, 0.0375] and ends at [0.0, 0.0375]. The fourth line starts at [0.0, 0.0375] and ends at [0.0, 0.0]. After drawing the loop, apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the two-dimensional sketch. Rotate the scaled sketch using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, -90.0] and translate it using the vector [0.0, 0.0375, 0.0]. Extrude the sketch 0.0375 units in the direction of the normal, ensuring not to extrude in the opposite direction. Finally, create a new solid body from the extruded sketch. The dimensions of the rectangular base are length 0.75, width 0.0375, and height 0.0375.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system transformation
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY").rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), -90).translate((0, 0.0375, 0))

# Create the sketch for the rectangular top
sketch = (
    workplane
    .lineTo(0.75, 0)  # line_1
    .lineTo(0.75, 0.0375)  # line_2
    .lineTo(0, 0.0375)  # line_3
    .lineTo(0, 0)  # line_4
    .close()  # Close the loop
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.0375)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder

# Display the final model

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0375, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0375, 0.0375) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0375) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
